pass_a_gloss: All the things written about God, even if they appear discordant at first glance, must be understood as worthy of the good God. For who will not say that things referred to God—that he has wrath, that he uses anger, that he regrets, and even that he sleeps—appear discordant? But each of these, for the one who knows how to hear dark words, will be found worthy of God. For his wrath is not barren, but as his word educates, so also his wrath educates; for those not educated by word he educates by wrath. And it is necessary that God use the so-called wrath, as he uses the so-named word; for his word is not such as the word of all. For no one’s word is 'a living being,' no one’s word is 'God,' no one’s word 'in the beginning' was toward that one whose the Word was. So also the wrath of God is called wrath not as the wrath of just anyone. And as the Word of God has something strange beside every word of just anyone—and has the strange thing of being God and being Word as living, of existing by itself, of serving the Father—so, once God’s so-called wrath was named, it has something strange and alien to every wrath of the one being defined. So also his anger has something of its own; for it is of the purpose of the anger that refutes, wanting the one refuted to turn through the refutation. Word also refutes, as word educates; but word does not refute as anger refutes. For those not benefited by the refutation from the word will need the refutation from the anger. We said that there is also a regret of God that appears discordant at first glance, since it is written: 'I have regretted that I anointed Saul as king.' And worthily you will seek also the regret, and you will not think his regret has any kinship with the regret of those who regret. For as his word had something exceptional, and his wrath something surpassing, and nothing was akin to these among the homonyms, in the same way his regret also is homonymous with our regret; and homonyms are those whose name alone is common, but the account according to the name of the substance is other. Therefore only the name is common of God’s anger and anyone’s anger, and only the name is common of anyone’s wrath and God’s wrath. So also upon regret it must be understood. And the one able will seek what God’s regret works, what it worked. It took down Saul reigning lawlessly; it raised up as king for the people the one according to God’s heart; for he said because of that good regret: 'I have found a man according to my heart, David son of Jesse.' pass_b_english: All the things written about God, even if they look discordant at first hearing, must be understood as worthy of the good God. Who will not say that things referred to God—that he has wrath, that he uses anger, that he regrets, even that he sleeps—look discordant? But each of these, for the one who knows how to hear dark words, will be found worthy of God.

For his wrath is not barren: as his word educates, so also his wrath educates; those not educated by word he educates by wrath. And it is necessary that God use the so-called wrath as he uses the so-named Word; for his Word is not such as everyone’s word. No one’s word is 'a living being,' no one’s word is 'God,' no one’s word was 'in the beginning' toward that one whose the Word was. So also God’s wrath is called wrath not as just anyone’s wrath. And as the Word of God has something strange beside every word of just anyone—being God, being Word as living, existing by itself, serving the Father—so once God’s so-called wrath was named, it has something strange and alien to every defined wrath.

So also his anger has something of its own; for it belongs to the purpose of the anger that refutes, wanting the one refuted to turn through the refutation. Word also refutes, as word educates; but word does not refute as anger refutes. Those not benefited by the refutation from the word will need the refutation from the anger. We said there is also a regret of God that looks discordant at first glance, since it is written: 'I have regretted that I anointed Saul as king.' (1 Samuel 15:11) Worthily seek also the regret, and do not think his regret has kinship with the regret of those who regret. As his Word had something exceptional, and his wrath something surpassing, and nothing was akin to these among the like-named, so also his regret is like-named with our regret; and like-named are those whose name alone is common, but the account of the substance according to the name is other. Therefore only the name is common of God’s anger and anyone’s anger, and only the name of anyone’s wrath and God’s wrath. So also upon regret. And the one able will seek what God’s regret works, what it worked. It took down Saul reigning lawlessly; it raised as king for the people the one according to God’s heart; for he said because of that good regret: 'I have found a man according to my heart, David son of Jesse.' (1 Samuel 13:14) But all these things are a preface for me (Jeremiah 20:7).
